chunks.title: Core Architectural Philosophy
chunks.summary: Defines strict boundaries, feature packaging, pure domain, central shared core, and the canonical dependency direction.
chunks.text: Strong architecture is usually strongest where it stays strict about boundaries. The main architectural ideas are package by feature, split each feature into domain, data, and presentation, keep domain pure Kotlin, make data implement domain contracts, keep UI dependent on domain, not on data internals, centralize cross-cutting concerns in shared/core/*, and use physical Gradle modules to enforce dependency direction. Canonical dependency rule: Presentation -> Domain <- Data.

chunks.title: Feature Module Template
chunks.summary: Defines domain, data, and presentation responsibilities and the presentation mapper rule.
chunks.text: Feature modules should be split into domain, data, and presentation. Domain contains models, repository interfaces, use cases, domain errors, and pure business rules, and must not contain Compose, platform APIs, Room, Ktor clients, or DataStore. Data contains repository implementations, DAO usage, DTOs, mappers, remote calls, local caching, and exception-to-domain-error mapping. Presentation contains screens, composables, UI models, mapper classes from domain to UI, view models, and only necessary platform UI effects.

chunks.title: Dependency Rules To Keep
chunks.summary: Defines strict dependency direction, aggregator exception, and warns against cross-feature data coupling.
chunks.text: Feature domain depends only on pure shared core modules. Feature data depends on its own domain plus shared runtime infrastructure. Feature presentation depends on its own domain, shared presentation helpers, and design system. Feature presentation modules should not depend on other feature presentation modules. Aggregator-style features may depend on other features' domain modules only. Cross-feature data-module coupling should be treated as an exception, not a standard.

chunks.title: Domain Layer Practices
chunks.summary: Defines pure domain, typed result modeling, cancellation-safe suspend result helpers, use case naming, and time access through TimeProvider.
chunks.text: Domain should remain platform-agnostic and framework-light. Domain models describe business meaning, not storage shape. Repository interfaces live in domain and implementations live in data. Use typed result wrappers for domain-facing operations and define domain-specific error hierarchies. Shared suspend result helpers should preserve structured concurrency by rethrowing CancellationException and mapping only real failures. Domain and feature code must not call Clock.System.now() directly; time flows through TimeProvider.

chunks.title: Data Layer Practices
chunks.summary: Defines repository translation boundaries, cancellation-safe helpers, cache-first reads, shared Room builder setup, per-feature clients, and mapper placement.
chunks.text: Repositories translate external systems into domain-safe behavior. They map DTOs and entities into domain models, convert infrastructure failures into domain errors, and expose domain-friendly return types. Repository helpers must always rethrow CancellationException. Prefer local cache as the first read path when appropriate. Common Room builder setup belongs in shared/core/database so feature data modules do not duplicate bundled SQLite driver or KMP-safe query dispatcher policy. Data modules that talk to a backend should own a named HttpClient unless there is a strong reason to share one. Mapping should stay near the boundary, with data mapping in data and domain-to-UI mapping in presentation.

chunks.title: Presentation Layer Practices
chunks.summary: Defines state/action/event separation, a small lifecycle-backed MVI base, sequential action handling, explicit initial loading, and consistent presentation structure.
chunks.text: Presentation should separate UiState, UiAction, and UiEvent. A base MVI view model should stay small and practical, extend lifecycle ViewModel when screen state is long-lived, and process rapid actions through a single sequential queue. Initial loading and retry behavior should be explicit and testable from stable lifecycle-aware entry points. Observation pipelines should be grouped by business concern. Prefer one consistent presentation pattern across the app, using the shared MVI base unless there is a compelling reason not to.

chunks.title: Navigation Practices
chunks.summary: Defines app shell ownership, Navigation 3 typed routes, canonical route ownership, Navigator back stack ownership, Koin entry providers, and top-level route separation.
chunks.text: A root app shell should own app-wide navigation, theme application, and safe-area handling. Navigation 3 routes should be typed values, such as SampleRoute implementing AppRoute, and the top-level route hierarchy should live in one shared presentation/core module instead of being duplicated in navigation. Shared navigation should expose a small Navigator that owns the back stack and renders it with NavDisplay. Compose UI modules should register Koin Navigation 3 entries with navigation<Route> { ... } and retrieve screen dependencies at the navigation entry boundary. Feature modules should stay free of global route dependencies unless they own the destination or a nested graph.

chunks.title: Resource And Localization Practices
chunks.summary: Defines shared/core/strings Compose Resources, no hardcoded user-visible strings, public Res export, and a canonical Res import path.
chunks.text: Shared user-visible strings should come from the dedicated shared/core/strings Compose Resources module. Shared UI code should not hardcode user-visible strings. Resource modules that are consumed across module boundaries should export the generated Res class publicly. One canonical Res import path should be defined and used consistently across modules, such as com.dream.template.shared.core.strings.Res for template strings.

chunks.title: Dependency Injection Practices
chunks.summary: Defines top-level DI startup, non-Compose core registrations, UI-owned navigation and ViewModel registrations, constructor injection, and explicit platform service injection.
chunks.text: startKoin should be called only from top-level app initialization paths. Non-Compose shared modules provide domain/data registrations, UI modules provide navigation, screen, and view-model registrations, platform startup paths provide platform factories, and composition roots assemble everything without making exported core modules depend on Compose. Constructor injection is the default. Lifecycle ViewModels should be registered through Koin's dedicated view-model DSL and retrieved from Compose through koinViewModel() instead of being built from rememberCoroutineScope(). Platform services should be injected through shared interfaces instead of reaching across boundaries directly.

chunks.title: Testing-Oriented Practices
chunks.summary: Defines reusable testing anchors such as injected time, explicit repository boundaries, and shared test utilities in shared/core/testing.
chunks.text: Keep domain pure, inject time, and use explicit repository interfaces with typed results to reduce mocking complexity. Shared fake providers and coroutine-aware helpers should live in shared/core/testing so features can reuse one test infrastructure baseline. Test feature behavior at the feature layer and queue semantics at the shared presentation layer.

chunks.title: Default Rules And Anti-Patterns
chunks.summary: Defines default rules for future projects and the main anti-patterns to avoid.
chunks.text: Default rules include feature-based modules, Presentation -> Domain <- Data, pure Kotlin domain, smaller shared core modules, TimeProvider as the centralized time source, shared design system and strings, repository typed results, and shared business logic with platform implementations behind interfaces. Anti-patterns include casual cross-feature data coupling, raw preference parsing in UI or domain, direct system time usage, hardcoded shared UI strings, leaked route types, giant convention plugins, over-opinionated design systems, and overbuilt MVI frameworks.

chunks.title: Package And App Identity Practices
chunks.summary: Defines canonical app identity derivation, immediate normalization of package-defining surfaces, and explicit rename audits.
chunks.text: Dream should derive one canonical app identity before renaming anything, then normalize package roots, namespaces, application ids, and visible app identity from that source of truth. Generated projects should record an explicit rename audit across Gradle names, module namespaces, package declarations, manifests, iOS identity, Desktop app titles when Desktop is included in the app contract, and .mvp metadata.

chunks.title: Stable Composition Root Practices
chunks.summary: Defines stable dependency assembly outside recomposing composables, explicit initial loading, and DI-managed ViewModel retrieval at root composables.
chunks.text: Repositories, use cases, and ViewModels should be assembled at stable roots such as app initialization, coordinators, or factories, not created inside recomposing composables. Root composables should stay orchestration-focused, initial loading should not rely on unstable repeated construction paths, and root composables may retrieve DI-managed ViewModels but should not construct repositories or coroutine scopes to manufacture them.

chunks.title: UI Quality And State Design Practices
chunks.summary: Defines state-specific UX expectations, shared-token usage, and intentional loading, empty, content, and error state quality.
chunks.text: Dream should define user-facing expectations for loading, empty, content, and error states in the contract and review them before approval. Feature screens should use shared tokens instead of ad hoc sizing, and state handling should feel intentional rather than placeholder-level.
